source_refs.note: Book p. 199-200: 6.5 Hyperbola, definition, Figure 6.21, Derivation of the Standard Equation of Hyperbola with Figure 6.22 (up to the start of 6.5.1)

blocks.text: Bachon, ellipse ke baad ab hum us ke 'judwan bhai' hyperbola ko parhte hain. Dono ki bunyaad ek hi hai: do fixed points (foci) aur ek chalta hua point \(P\). Farq sirf ek lafz ka hai. Ellipse mein \(P\) se dono foci tak ke faaslon ka jor (sum) fixed rehta hai, jab ke hyperbola mein in faaslon ka farq (difference) fixed rehta hai, aur woh bhi absolute value mein, yani minus ka nishaan hata kar. Is ek tabdeeli ka nateeja yeh hai ke hyperbola ka graph do alag alag hisson mein bant jata hai; in hisson ko branches (shaakhein) kehte hain (Figure 6.21 dekhiye).

Is section mein hum teen kaam karenge. Pehle hyperbola ki definition ko achhi tarah samjhenge, yani kaun se points is curve par aate hain aur kyun. Phir isi definition se, sirf distance formula aur thori si algebra laga kar, hyperbola ki standard equation khud nikalenge. Aakhir mein dekhenge ke \(a\), \(b\) aur \(c\) ka aapas mein kya rishta hai. Yeh derivation lamba lagta hai magar har qadam mein sirf ek hi kaam hota hai; aap har line ke saath 'kyun' poochte jaiye to sab asaan lagega. Exam mein yeh derivation bhi aa sakta hai, is liye isay ratne ke bajaye samajhna zaroori hai.

blocks.text: Kitab mein "see Figure 21" chhapa hai; asal mein Figure 6.21 ki baat ho rahi hai (neeche di gayi hai).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Socho do mobile towers hain, ek \(F'\) par aur ek \(F\) par. Aap aisi jagah khare hain jahan se \(F'\) wala tower, \(F\) wale tower se hamesha theek 6 km zyada door hai. Aisi tamaam jagahon ko jor dein to ek branch banti hai. Aur jahan \(F\) wala tower 6 km zyada door ho, woh doosri branch hai. Yahi hyperbola hai. Purane zamane mein jahaz isi usool se apni position maloom karte the (do radio stations ke signals ke waqt ke farq se). Neeche table mein ellipse aur hyperbola ka muqabla diya gaya hai; poora section parhte hue isay saamne rakhiye.

Foci se faaslon ka farq (difference) fixed: \(\big||PF'| - |PF|\big| = 2a\)

blocks.text: Derivation of the Standard Equation of Hyperbola

Ab hum hyperbola ki saaf definition likhte hain: hyperbola un tamaam points \((x, y)\) ka set hai jin ke do alag fixed points (foci) se faaslon ke farq ki absolute value constant ho. Sab se saada equation tab milti hai jab foci kisi ek coordinate axis par hon. Is liye hum foci ko \(x\)-axis par \(F'(-c, 0)\) aur \(F(c, 0)\) par rakhte hain, taa ke origin dono foci ke bilkul beech (midpoint) mein aa jaye (Figure 6.22). Yeh bilkul waisa hi intikhab hai jaisa humne ellipse mein kiya tha: symmetry se hisaab aasaan ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "hyper bola" do tukron mein chhapa hai; sahi lafz ek hai: hyperbola. Jumla yun hona chahiye: "Thus, we can define a hyperbola as the set of all points \((x, y)\) ...". Aur "Figure 22" se muraad Figure 6.22 hai (neeche).

blocks.alt: Coordinate axes par hyperbola jo baayen aur daayen khulti hai. Foci F'(-c, 0) aur F(c, 0) x-axis par, origin O dono ke beech, aur daayen branch par point P(x, y) dono foci se jura hua.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.22: Foci F'(-c, 0), F(c, 0) aur hyperbola ka point P(x, y) (kitab ki figure ke mutabiq hamari apni drawing)

blocks.text:
Maan lijiye hyperbola ke kisi bhi point \(P(x, y)\) se dono foci tak ke faaslon ke farq ki absolute value \(2a\) hai, jahan \(a > 0\). Yani
\[\big||PF'| - |PF|\big| = 2a\]
ya
\[|PF'| - |PF| = \pm 2a\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Constant ko \(2a\) kyun kaha, sirf \(a\) kyun nahi? Is liye ke aage chal kar vertices \(x = \pm a\) par aate hain, bilkul ellipse ki tarah, aur formulas chhote rehte hain.
Aur \(\pm\) kyun? Agar \(P\) daayen branch par hai to woh \(F\) ke qareeb hai, is liye \(|PF'| - |PF| = +2a\). Agar baayen branch par hai to \(F'\) ke qareeb hai aur farq \(-2a\) aata hai. \(\pm\) likh kar hum dono branches ek saath sambhal lete hain.

Ab distance formula lagate hain. \(P(x, y)\) se \(F'(-c, 0)\) tak faasla \(\sqrt{(x+c)^2 + y^2}\) aur \(F(c, 0)\) tak \(\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\) hai. Is liye
\[\sqrt{(x+c)^2 + y^2} - \sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]
\[= \pm 2a\]

Is equation mein do square roots hain. Agar hum seedha square karein to cross term mein phir root aa jayega. Is liye pehle ek root ko akela ek taraf karte hain, phir square karte hain:
\[\sqrt{(x+c)^2 + y^2}\]
\[= \pm 2a + \sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]

Dono taraf square karne par (right side par \((p + q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2\) ka formula laga):
\[(x+c)^2 + y^2\]
\[= 4a^2 \pm 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]
\[\quad + (x-c)^2 + y^2\]

Ab brackets kholte hain:
\[x^2 + 2cx + c^2 + y^2\]
\[= 4a^2 \pm 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]
\[\quad + x^2 - 2cx + c^2 + y^2\]

Dekhiye, \(x^2\), \(c^2\) aur \(y^2\) dono taraf maujood hain, is liye yeh cancel ho jate hain:
\[2cx = 4a^2 \pm 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]
\[\quad - 2cx\]

\(cx\) wale terms ko ek jagah ikattha karte hain (\(-2cx\) ko left par le gaye to \(+2cx\) ban gaya):
\[4cx = 4a^2 \pm 4a\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2}\]

Ab 4 se divide karte hain aur bache hue root ko akela karte hain:
\[\mp a\sqrt{(x-c)^2 + y^2} = a^2 - cx\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Root ko akela karna kyun zaroori tha? \(\sqrt{A} - \sqrt{B}\) ka seedha square karein to \(-2\sqrt{AB}\) wala term aata hai jis mein root ab bhi maujood hai. Jab root akela ho to ek hi square se woh poora khatam ho jata hai. Isi liye do dafa square karna parta hai: har dafa ek root ko akela kar ke.
Aur \(\mp\) kahan se aaya? \(4cx = 4a^2 \pm 4a\sqrt{\cdots}\) ko 4 se divide karein to \(cx - a^2 = \pm a\sqrt{\cdots}\). Root wale term ko doosri taraf le jane se us ka sign ulat jata hai, to \(\pm\) ban jata hai \(\mp\). Agle square ke baad yeh sign khud hi khatam ho jayega, kyun ke minus ka square bhi plus hota hai.

Ab doosri dafa dono taraf square karte hain. Left par \(a^2\) aur bracket ka square, right par \((a^2 - cx)^2 = a^4 - 2a^2cx + c^2x^2\):
\[a^2[(x-c)^2 + y^2]\]
\[= a^4 - 2a^2cx + c^2x^2\]

Dono taraf \(-2a^2cx\) maujood hai; dono taraf \(2a^2cx\) jama karne se yeh khatam ho jata hai:
\[a^2x^2 + a^2c^2 + a^2y^2 = a^4 + c^2x^2\]

Ab \(x^2\) wale terms ek taraf aur constants doosri taraf rakhte hain, phir common factor nikalte hain:
\[a^2x^2 - c^2x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^4 - a^2c^2\]
\[(a^2 - c^2)x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^2(a^2 - c^2)\]

Ab Figure 6.22 ke triangle \(PF'F\) ko dekhiye. Triangle ki kisi do sides ka farq teesri side se kam hota hai, is liye \(|PF'| - |PF| < |F'F|\), yani \(2a < 2c\). Is se \(a < c\) aur nateeja \(a^2 - c^2 < 0\), yani yeh quantity negative hai. Negative quantity ke saath kaam asaan karne ke liye hum ek naya constant \(b\) banate hain: \(-b^2 = a^2 - c^2\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein yahan "Figure 2" likha hai; muraad Figure 6.22 hai, jahan triangle \(PF'F\) bana hua hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh triangle inequality hai: kisi bhi triangle mein ek side doosri do sides ke farq se hamesha lambi hoti hai. Ghar se school aur ghar se dukaan ke raston ka farq kabhi school se dukaan ke seedhe faasle se zyada nahi ho sakta. Isi wajah se hyperbola mein \(c\) hamesha \(a\) se bara hota hai, jab ke ellipse mein ulta tha (\(a > c\)).
Is ko upar wali equation mein rakhne se hyperbola ki equation yeh ban jati hai: \((-b^2)x^2 + a^2y^2 = a^2(-b^2)\).

Aakhir mein dono taraf \(-a^2b^2\) se divide karte hain. \(-b^2x^2\) divide ho kar \(\frac{x^2}{a^2}\) banta hai, \(a^2y^2\) divide ho kar \(-\frac{y^2}{b^2}\), aur right side 1 ban jati hai. Yun hyperbola ki standard equation milti hai:

blocks.text_alt: x squared over a squared minus y squared over b squared equals 1

blocks.text: Is equation ko parhna seekhiye. \(x^2\) wala term positive hai, is liye curve \(x\)-axis ki taraf khulti hai, yani baayen aur daayen. \(y = 0\) rakhein to \(x = \pm a\), yani curve \(x\)-axis ko \((\pm a, 0)\) par kaat-ti hai; yeh vertices hain. \(x = 0\) rakhein to \(y^2 = -b^2\), jo kisi real number ke liye mumkin nahi, is liye curve \(y\)-axis ko kabhi nahi chhooti. Yahi wajah hai ke beech mein khali jagah reh jati hai aur do branches banti hain. \(a\) vertex ka faasla hai, \(c\) focus ka faasla hai, aur \(b\) un dono ko jorne wala number hai: \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\). In sab baaton ko agle section 6.5.1 mein tafseel se dekhenge.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(b\) kyun banaya? Kyun ke \(a^2 - c^2\) negative hai, aur us ko \(-b^2\) (jahan \(b > 0\)) likhne se equation bilkul saaf shakal mein aa jati hai.
Yaad rakhne ka aasaan tareeqa: ellipse mein equation mein plus \(\left(\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\right)\) aur relation mein minus \((c^2 = a^2 - b^2)\). Hyperbola mein equation mein minus aur relation mein plus \((c^2 = a^2 + b^2)\). Yani dono jagah sign ulat jata hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Ek number wali misaal se formula ko parakhte hain. \(a = 3\), \(c = 5\) lijiye. To \(b^2 = 25 - 9 = 16\) aur hyperbola \(\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1\) hai. Point \(P\left(5, \frac{16}{3}\right)\) is par hai, kyun ke \(\frac{25}{9} - \frac{256}{144} = \frac{25}{9} - \frac{16}{9} = 1\). Ab foci \(F(5, 0)\) aur \(F'(-5, 0)\) se faasle:
\[|PF| = \dfrac{16}{3}\]
\[|PF'| = \sqrt{100 + \dfrac{256}{9}} = \dfrac{34}{3}\]
Farq \(\frac{34}{3} - \frac{16}{3} = \frac{18}{3} = 6\) hai, jo bilkul \(2a = 6\) hai. Definition sach nikli!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(2a = 2c\) hota, yani faaslon ka farq foci ke darmiyani faasle ke barabar ho, to kya hota? Tab \(P\) sirf \(x\)-axis ke us hisse par ho sakta jo foci se bahar hai (do rays), koi curve nahi banti. Aur \(2a > 2c\) mumkin hi nahi (triangle inequality). Is liye hyperbola ke liye \(a < c\) zaroori hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Agar exam mein 'derive the standard equation of hyperbola' aaye to pehle figure banaiye aur foci \(F'(-c, 0)\), \(F(c, 0)\) likhiye. Phir definition \(|PF'| - |PF| = \pm 2a\) likh kar distance formula lagaiye. Har squaring se pehle saaf likhiye ke kaun sa root akela kiya. Triangle inequality wali line (\(a < c\)) aur \(-b^2 = a^2 - c^2\) wali line zaroor likhiye; yahi do lines aksar students chhor dete hain aur un ke marks kat jate hain. Aakhir mein \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) likhna mat bhooliye.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Hyperbola: \(\big||PF'| - |PF|\big| = 2a\), yani foci se faaslon ka farq constant.
2. Foci \((\pm c, 0)\) hon to \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\), jahan \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).
3. Triangle inequality se \(a < c\).
4. Graph ki do alag branches hoti hain.
5. Derivation ka tareeqa: ek root akela karo, square karo, saada karo, doosra root akela karo, phir square karo.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Hyperbola mein \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) likh dena. Yeh ellipse ka relation hai; hyperbola mein \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\).
2. Yeh kehna ke faaslon ka jor constant hai. Hyperbola mein farq (absolute value mein) constant hota hai.
3. \(\sqrt{A} - \sqrt{B} = 2a\) ka root akela kiye baghair seedha square kar dena; roots khatam nahi hote aur hisaab ulajh jata hai.
4. Bhool jana ke \(|PF'| - |PF|\) ki value \(+2a\) bhi ho sakti hai aur \(-2a\) bhi (har branch ka apna sign).
